q: What CBAM figure does an EU buyer need for Algerian clinker?
title: Algerian clinker: the CBAM figure
short: Per tonne of clinker: calcination CO2 from limestone, roughly half a tonne, plus kiln fuel, which in Algeria is mostly gas. Electricity counts for cement too. Ask for a verified figure; gas fired kilns can come in below the EU default.
audience: EU importers and traders buying clinker and cement from Algerian plants

ul: Bought clinker if a plant buys from another.

p: Cement adds grinding power and takes the clinker share times its figure. Ask for the clinker share of each grade.
Algeria has no carbon price to deduct.

senseible: Senseible keeps each site's fuel, power and production records together, so the embedded emissions you send an EU importer trace back to dated documents.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
